title: The Random Promoter DREAM Challenge 2022's test set: 71,103 promoter sequences of 110 bases (80 random or designed bases between fixed flanks) with their expression measured in yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) by sorting and sequencing, estimated with MAUDE
provider: de Boer lab (University of British Columbia) and the DREAM Challenges; Rafi et al., Nature Biotechnology (2025), data on Zenodo, record 10633252
credit: Promoter expression: Random Promoter DREAM Challenge (Rafi et al. 2025)
format: Text, one promoter per line: the sequence (110 bases: the flank TGCATTTTTTTCACATC, 80 variable bases, the flank GGTTACGGCTGTT) and its expression, tab-separated. The expression is MAUDE's estimate from sorting cells into bins by a fluorescent reporter, a log-scale value (from -1.40 to 1.66 in this file; mean 0.16, standard deviation 0.75). The test set mixes random sequences, native yeast promoters, designed sequences of high and low expression, single-nucleotide variants of them and motif perturbations (the challenge's subsets, which this file does not label), so that many sequences are near copies of others: a model's held-out evaluation must keep such families on one side of the split.
coverage: 71,103 sequences, the challenge's filtered test set (training data, 6.7 million sequences in train.txt of the same record, not fetched)
licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), as the Zenodo record states.
